Angiotensin I and II is a part of the Renin-Angiotensin-System (RAS) in the kidneys. Angiotensin I is converted to Angiotensin II by ACE (Angiotensin Converting Enzyme). Angiotensin II is a potent vasocontractor and it also stimulates the release of aldosterone. So ACE-I block the production of Angiotensin II, which leads to a reduction in blood pressure.

The levator palpebrae superioris muscle is innervated by the occulomotor nerve (III) at a synapse in the superior orbital fissure. However, in the event of an occulomotor (III) lesion, the patient will use the spare innervation of the levator palpebrae muscle from the facial nerve to open the eye - hence, the degree of eye opening is less than that of a total ptosis. The orbicularis oculi muscle is innervated by the facial nerve (VII) and is responsible for closing the eye. The upper eyelid reflex (light touch) involves the facial nerve (VII) and the occulomotor nerve (III) - the facial nerve (VII) innervates the orbicularis oculi and the occulomotor nerve (III) innervates the levator palpebrae superioris.
